rows.title_short: Comprehensive Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act
rows.abstract: \"Comprehensive Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act.\" The bill raises the age of criminal responsibility from 9 to 12 years old. It seeks to restore the harm done to victims and, at the same time, give youth offenders the chance to be rehabilitated and be integrated into society. It establishes the Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Protection and the Children's Ombudsman.

rows.abstract: The bill increases the monthly minimum wage of househelpers from P800 to P3,000 in highly urbanized cities; from P650 to P1,000 in other chartered cities and 1st class municipalities; and from P550 to P800 in other municipalities.

rows.abstract: \"An Act Amending LOI 745 and Prescribing the Penalties Therefor.\" The bill provides standard basic dive rules to all levels/kinds of divers, regulate the sport and expand the powers of existing governmental agencies in order to further promote the sport and protect the safety of its enthusiasts.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO LEGALIZE CHURCH DECLARATION OF NULLITY OR NON-EXISTENCE, ANNULMENT OR DISSOLUTION OF CERTAIN MARRIAGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill provides that when a marriage, legally solemnized by a priest, minister, imam, rabbi or presiding elder of an established church, is subsequently declared null or non-existent, annulled or dissolved in a final judgment or decree by said church or religion in accordance with the cannons of the latter, duly entered in the corresponding civil registry, the said declaration shall be recognized and given full force and effect in the Philippines.

rows.abstract: \"Fuel Ethanol Act of 2004.\" The bill provides for the use of ethanol as an alternative fuel through the Fuel Ethanol Program. The Program shall launch the production of unconventional and replenishable sources of energy and fuel.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PRESENTATION TO THE PRESS OR PUBLIC OF SUSPECTS IN CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS BEFORE CASES ARE FORMALLY FILED AGAINST THE SUSPECTS
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to hold any person criminally, civilly and administratively liable for presenting a suspect, who is being investigated, publicly or in a press conference. It also proposes certain guideliness on what the police can do to keep the public informed as to the status of pending high-profile cases.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06046

rows.title_full: AN ACT LIMITING THE HOURS OF CASINO OPERATIONS FROM TEN (10) A.M. TO TWO (2) A.M., AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 14 SUBPARAGRAPH 2 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1869
rows.abstract: The bill provides for casino operations to start from 10:00 a.m. up to 2:00 a.m. In places where curfew hours are imposed, all players and personnel of the casinos must leave the casino premises before the curfew hours start.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GAMES AND AMUSEMENTS since 2004-11-08

rows.abstract: \"Additional Teachers' Insurance Act of 2004.\" The bill grants public school teachers the following term insurance coverage: a) P100,000 death benefits; b) P50,000 burial expenses; and c) P100,000 reimbursement of actual medical expenses.

rows.abstract: \"Botica sa Barangay Act.\" The bill enjoins the Department of Health to put up drugstores in every barangay making drugs for common illnesses readily available.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEMATIC AND PERIODIC REVIEW OF THE ECONOMY, EFFICIENCY AND VIABILITY OF GOVERNMENT-OWNED OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Sunset Act of 2004.\" The bill provides a mechanism for the systematic review and evaluation of government-owned and controlled corporations (GOCCs). It empowers the committees of the Senate and the House of Representatives having legislative jurisdiction over GOCCs to regularly conduct sunset reviews on these GOCCs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2004-11-08

rows.abstract: The bill provides for the punong barangay to be appointed by the Governor from a list of 3 nominees submitted by the Representative of the district where the barangay belongs and for the barangay kagawads to be appointed by the Mayor from a list of 2 nominees for each kagawad position submitted by the minority and majority members of the sangguniang panglungsod.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR MANDATORY TRAINING ON HUMAN RIGHTS FOR ALL OFFICERS, MEMBERS AND TRAINEES OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES (AFP), THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE (PNP), THE NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION (NBI), AND OTHER LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES, AS WELL AS OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES IN THE EXECUTIVE, LEGISLATIVE AND JUDICIAL BRANCHES OF GOVERNMENT INCLUDING GOVERNMENT-OWNED AND/OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill requires all branches of the government to include the study of human rights in the education and training of their officers and employees. It also directs all government-owned or financed training institutions to include in their curricula a regular course on human rights.

rows.abstract: \"Commission on Human Rights Act of 2004.\" The bill provides for an expanded structural and functional organization to enable the Commission to meet the demands of human rights cases here and abroad.
